<b>Ductsuckers</b> are [[Enemies (Silksong)|enemies]] in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i>. They are large, worm-like creatures sustained by the thick slime coating their caves.<ref>Ductsucker [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"Suction creature surviving on the thick slime that coats its caves."</i></ref>

== Behaviour and Tactics ==
Ductsuckers start out moving slowly along aqueducts, gutturally roaring as soon as [[Hornet (Silksong)|Hornet]] approaches and beginning a ferocious onslaught using the following attacks:
* <b>Charge:</b> Charges towards Hornet, turning around with poor traction as soon as she gets behind it or it reaches an edge. It can turn around up to three times before choosing a different move.
* <b>Leap:</b> Roars and then leaps at Hornet, an attack easily dodged by moving underneath it. If it has enough space and Hornet isn't behind it, it Leaps a second time. It often uses Charge immediately after its final Leap if Hornet is still in front of it. Occasionally, a Ductsucker may leap off the edge of an aqueduct and fall into the water, but this does not count as a kill for the [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]]. After roughly 15 seconds, it returns to the platform, emerging from the ground.
* <b>Burrow:</b> Quickly dives into the ground, then pokes its mouth out beneath Hornet 1–2 times, indicated by green particles kicking up below her. Once finished, it resurfaces somewhere along its aqueduct segment. It cannot use this move twice in a row.
If Hornet becomes fully unreachable, the Ductsucker immediately burrows and returns to its slow-moving state somewhere on the aqueduct.

All of the Ductsuckers' attacks, including contact damage, deal {{Damage|2}}.

Stationary traps like [[Tacks]] or [[Sting Shard]]s are highly effective for dealing damage without getting too close. The [[Curveclaw]] also works exceptionally well due to the Ductsucker's size, allowing it to land multiple hits in a single strike.
